scope: Versioned feature/API inventory. Status is scoped to the exact row; neither passing negative probes nor builtin-name availability measure overall Python coverage.

features.scope: Unicode identifiers normalized with pinned Unicode data; Unicode strings, raw/triple strings, explicit/implicit line joining and indentation within core-source/1.
features.gaps: The exact admitted grammar is documented in interpreter-language.md; other literal families have separate rows.

features.scope: Arbitrary integers, binary64 real and owned complex values; exact integer true division, bounded powers, bitwise/shifts and primitive helpers; real/complex construction and selected numeric/index callbacks. Both source profiles admit primitive APIs; callbacks require classes-source/1.
features.gaps: General complex powers, non-finite complex arithmetic/intermediate recovery and numeric methods remain INT-NUM-02. Broader class arithmetic and formatting remain separate.

features.scope: Unicode code-point length, concatenation, comparison, membership, indexing and slicing, including negative step.
features.gaps: General string methods, formatting and bytes/encoding APIs are not adopted.

features.scope: List/tuple/dict literals, item access/mutation, scalar list deletion, primitive reads, list append/aliases/in-place operations and primitive-key dictionary equivalence/order; classes-source/1 also admits bounded list/tuple RHS slice assignment/deletion. Classes-source/1 also adopts user/default dictionary keys and owned list/tuple/dictionary equality. Finite list/tuple construction preserves primitive and owned iterable elements; user length hints remain refused. Set/frozenset construction, displays, owned membership/equality, finite mutation APIs and primitive algebra are adopted.
features.gaps: Dictionary constructors, broader methods, structural dictionary comparison mutation and remaining value/hash families are deferred.

features.scope: Admitted expression evaluation, chained comparisons, identity/membership, short circuit and/or, not and conditional expressions.
features.gaps: This row covers admitted value/protocol families, not every Python expression.

features.scope: if/elif/else, while/for over adopted values, loop else/break/continue, return and finally control transfer.
features.gaps: Generator, context-manager, match and async control are separate rows.

features.scope: def, recursion, positional-only/ordinary/keyword-only parameters; literal and definition-time computed/mutable defaults and lexical closures. Global/nonlocal writes and deletion share the defining module and lexical cells. Variadic positional/keyword parameters pack fresh owned values. Positional starred calls consume owned iterables. Keyword call expansion admits owned dictionaries and keys/getitem mappings with ordered duplicate checks.
features.gaps: Construction-hint forms and annotations remain deferred; signatures and error-message comparisons are scoped by interpreter-function-binding.md.

features.scope: Assertions and assignment expressions in both source profiles, with owned truth callbacks and lexical scope writes. Lambda functions use ordinary parameters/defaults and lexical cells. Tuple/list/starred assignments, loop targets, and starred sequence/dictionary displays use owned iteration/mapping phases.
features.gaps: Construction hints remain with their sequence task; assertion message formatting and comprehensions retain separate gates.

features.scope: Explicit classes-source/1 only: user classes, bounded C3 MRO, __init__, ordinary attributes/deletion and bound methods.
features.gaps: Builtin subclassing, __new__, super, metaclasses, implicit __class__ cells and full reflective behavior are not adopted. Builtin list/tuple bases are explicitly refused with UNSUPPORTED.

features.scope: Lexical private-name mangling in admitted class bodies, nested code, parameters/imports and metadata.
features.gaps: No additional syntax beyond the explicit source profile.

features.scope: Functions, properties, static/class methods, custom get/set/delete/name-notification descriptors and decorators in classes-source/1.
features.gaps: Descriptor-valued setter/deleter/name-notification hooks and unrestricted reflection remain refused.

features.scope: Type-level __call__/__len__/__bool__, callable(), len(), bool(), not and control tests in classes-source/1, including adopted descriptor binding and optional truth fallback.
features.gaps: Length uses the explicit signed-64-bit contract; later protocols remain separate.

features.scope: print/str display None, bool, int, strings and adopted exception messages; str() and str(s) preserve the adopted identity rules. repr covers None/bool/int/str and explicit user __repr__; type-level __str__/__repr__ callbacks and print sequencing run on the owned machine.
features.gaps: Float/container/default-object displays, exception repr, format specifications and unadopted str/print keyword or encoding forms remain deferred.

features.scope: __index__/__getitem__/__setitem__/__delitem__ through current type lookup and owned callbacks; raw scalar/tuple/slice keys, builtin sequence conversion, __len__ index results and bounded list/tuple RHS slice mutation.
features.gaps: Other iterable RHS slice assignment, slice repr/hash/indices, builtin subclasses and broader numeric/sequence APIs remain deferred.

features.scope: Owned __iter__/__next__/__contains__, indexed fallback, iter/next signatures and iterator membership search in classes-source/1.
features.gaps: Generators/async protocols, broader iterable-consuming APIs and ordering remain separate.

features.scope: Owned __eq__/__ne__/__hash__, NotImplemented, reflected priority, bounded container equality and user dictionary keys.
features.gaps: Structural dictionary mutation during comparison, tuples containing user instances, bound-method/slice hashing and ordering remain separately gated.

features.scope: Arithmetic/reflected/in-place slots, __new__, metaclasses, custom attribute hooks and builtin subclassing.
features.gaps: Each slice requires an adopted reference and owned continuation contract.

features.scope: Adopted builtin exception classes, catch/raise/bare reraise, try/except/else/finally, active context and source tracebacks.
features.gaps: Custom exception inheritance, explicit causes/suppression and exception groups/except* remain deferred.

features.scope: Static absolute/relative imports from a finite granted source registry, packages, identity/cache, initialization order, cycles and failed-init retry.
features.gaps: No ambient filesystem/sys.path/PyPI loader, dynamic __import__ or import hooks. Missing grants raise IMPORT/ImportError; that is an authority boundary, not proof of a missing language API.

features.scope: yield/yield from, generator methods, list/dict/set/generator comprehensions and suspended ownership.
features.gaps: No admitted generator or comprehension syntax.

features.scope: with and synchronous context manager protocols; match/case patterns and guards.
features.gaps: No admitted source execution. Async context managers are a separate async gate.

features.scope: Python 3.14 annotation timing, type parameters, type aliases and required generic aliases.
features.gaps: Annotations and generic syntax are not adopted. Recognized type aliases receive UNSUPPORTED without execution support.

features.scope: f-strings and formatting grammar; t-strings, Template/Interpolation and string.templatelib APIs.
features.gaps: Tokenizer rejects these literal forms. Server-side t-string use by a consumer does not establish browser interpreter support.

features.scope: Native coroutine/await semantics, async iteration/generators/context managers and bounded scheduling/cancellation.
features.gaps: Owned instruction stepping is implemented, but multiple parked owners, persistent events and native coroutine syntax are not. Host Promises are not Python coroutines.

features.scope: compile/eval/exec, dynamic imports and broader globals/locals/type/attribute reflection.
features.gaps: Source admission, namespace/identity and target authority need separate explicit contracts.

features.scope: core-only/1 has no library modules; operator/1 includes exactly add, sub, mul, floordiv, mod, eq, lt, neg, not_, truth, getitem from own Python source.
features.gaps: No whole-stdlib claim. json/math/random and licensed pure-Python colorsys API pilots require qualification. collections/itertools/functools/dataclasses/typing remain later API-selection decisions.

features.scope: A pinned package and exact entry-point use with source/resource/license closure, original/reduced differential execution and offline checks.
features.gaps: No general package certification. Shimify reachability is not interpreter compatibility; spatial_ui/expose_api and compiler integrations retain consumer-specific contracts.

features.scope: Offline browser worker with explicit source/assets/import grants; no ambient Python process/filesystem/network/device capabilities.
features.gaps: Durable sessions/storage, event/view adapters and one bounded awaited host capability remain under INT-10. Device inference needs separate real-device evidence in APP-MODEL-01.

features.scope: Independent JavaScript values and VM, with a separately planned C/Rust-to-Wasm backend.
features.gaps: No CPython C-extension ABI, native pointers, process/thread or arbitrary native module compatibility. A Wasm backend alone does not establish CPython ABI support.

features.scope: Reference oracle remains CPython 3.14.7; the live 3.14 documentation describes 3.14.9 at inventory adoption.
features.gaps: A documentation or build-Python update does not upgrade language support. Semantic/Unicode deltas and profile decisions require explicit tested adoption.

scope: Return an existing Python string unchanged from str(s), including closure-held and container-held aliases.
Compare source behavior with CPython 3.14.7 in Node and Chromium; cover rooting, resource failure and zero teardown. Update the compatibility observation and asset locks.
Recognize assignment expressions and type aliases as valid but unadopted forms, with UNSUPPORTED diagnostics and source spans.
Preserve SyntaxError for malformed source, no partial execution, all existing parser checks and a pinned source/refusal comparison for each form.
Compare current 3.14 maintenance documentation/changes with pinned CPython 3.14.7 and record relevant semantic deltas as executable cases.

Keep the existing oracle/profile until an explicit tested decision. Later Python minor versions require their own syntax, behavior, Unicode and profile decisions; documentation availability alone never upgrades support.
Specify type-slot lookup, descriptor binding, fallback precedence, actual-string return validation, print sequencing and nested output/error effects.

Author executable CPython 3.14.7 cases and explicit deferred cases for default object displays, float/container formatting and format specifications. Reference-only success must not claim engine support.
Adopt __repr__/__str__ for user instances, repr(None/bool/int/str), str() and the existing scalar str forms; retain explicit refusals for unadopted value families.

Use the owned operation machine, ordinary callback frames and exhaustive roots. Preserve print argument order and callback output, Python exceptions/source frames, stepping, cancellation, OOM and zero teardown.
Pin Unicode printability for string repr; include its complete generator/data/license and asset closure.
Add newly entered formatting source after offline reload, binding/body/result failures, pending-hook Stop/Restart and profile-update acceptance.
Update the compatibility inventory, source matrices, engine/asset locks, payload evidence and implementation plans. Keep the parent class milestone open for later protocols.
Specify and implement __index__, __getitem__, __setitem__ and __delitem__ through type lookup and owned continuations, including slice operands.
Test single evaluation, strict index results, mutation/alias effects, callback failures, resource interruption and teardown. Keep unadopted arithmetic slots refused.
Adopt __iter__, __next__, __contains__, StopIteration, iter(x), next(it, default), iter(callable, sentinel), for loops and indexed iteration fallback in a finite reference matrix.
Specify dispatch/fallback order and exception boundaries; verify paused loops, early exits, cancellation and roots. Async iteration is a separate milestone.

Specify int/float/complex constructors and complex arithmetic, integer true division, power and bitwise operators; abs, divmod, pow, round, bin, oct, hex, chr and ord with explicit supported signatures.
Adopt each API only with overflow, rounding, mixed-value, invalid-input and Node/browser source evidence. Arbitrary integers must not silently pass through lossy JavaScript numbers.
Adopt __eq__, __ne__, __hash__, NotImplemented and hash(), including subtype priority, hash disabling and dictionary invariants.
Separate identity hashing from serialized values; verify mutation, recursive callbacks, failed comparisons and resource teardown.
Adopt definition-time computed/mutable defaults, global/nonlocal writes, *args/**kwargs parameters and starred calls.
Preserve default identity, closure cells, single evaluation/order, duplicate keyword/binding errors and exception cleanup; record every supported signature with source cases.
Inventory and adopt exact signatures for list, tuple, dict, range, slice, enumerate, zip, reversed, all, any, sum, min, max, sorted, map and filter.

Add an explicit API table for string split/join/strip/replace/find, list append/extend/pop, tuple count/index and dict get/keys/values/items/update. Preserve aliasing, iteration order, callbacks and bounded work; anything outside that table remains deferred.
Specify set/frozenset and bytes/bytearray construction, literals and membership/index/slice behavior; explicitly scope memoryview to owned logical buffers.
Keep native memory addresses, process buffers and arbitrary host object access outside the value contract. Cover hashing, Unicode encoding errors, alias mutation and quotas.
Adopt assert, lambda, assignment expressions, tuple/list/starred assignment unpacking and starred collection displays.
Specify binding/evaluation order, short circuit behavior and malformed-versus-unsupported diagnostics; test actual source rather than fixture-only bytecode.
Specify generator construction, yield/yield from, send/throw/close and suspended ownership before admitting the syntax.

Adopt list/dict/set/generator comprehensions with Python scope and evaluation order. Cover finally, exhaustion, exceptions and cancellation. Coordinate parked ownership with #34 without requiring the full async application milestone.
Adopt with/__enter__/__exit__, multi-item and nested contexts with suppression/unwinding cases.
Separately adopt literal/capture/sequence/mapping/class/OR patterns, guards and bindings. Async context managers remain under #34.
Specify __new__, super, richer type/isinstance/issubclass, builtin subclassing and metaclass construction as separate reviewed protocol slices.

Adopt ExceptionGroup/BaseExceptionGroup and except* splitting/merging only after a reference matrix, including finally interactions and resource interruption.
